general_note: This tool reports observable signals on one page load. It does not decide whether a site complies with the law. Legal assessment depends on context, the full consent flow, and the applicable regulator's guidance.

refs.gdpr_4_11: GDPR Art. 4(11): consent must be freely given, specific, informed and unambiguous
refs.gdpr_7: GDPR Art. 7: conditions for consent, including that withdrawing consent must be as easy as giving it (Art. 7(3))
refs.gdpr_r32: GDPR Recital 32: consent requires a clear affirmative act; silence, pre-ticked boxes or inactivity do not constitute consent
refs.eprivacy_5_3: ePrivacy Directive Art. 5(3): storing or accessing information on a user's device requires consent unless strictly necessary
refs.pecr_6: PECR (UK) reg. 6: the UK implementation of the storage and access rule, with consent as defined in UK GDPR
refs.edpb_05_2020: EDPB Guidelines 05/2020 on consent under Regulation 2016/679
refs.edpb_03_2022: EDPB Guidelines 03/2022 on deceptive design patterns in social media platform interfaces (principles are often applied to consent interfaces more widely)
refs.planet49: CJEU, Planet49, Case C-673/17 (2019): pre-ticked checkboxes do not give valid consent for cookies

no_reject_option.title: No reject option on the first layer
no_reject_option.observed: A button that accepts cookies was found, but no button matching a reject wording was found on the first layer.
no_reject_option.not_observed: A reject-style button was found on the first layer.
no_reject_option.why: Consent has to be as easy to refuse as to give. A first layer that offers only acceptance, or acceptance plus a settings link, can make refusal harder.
no_reject_option.caution: Wording such as 'Accept only essential' is read as a non-reject by the matcher, and settings pages behind a link are not opened. A button inside an unusual component may be missed.

prechecked_box.title: Pre-ticked, enabled checkbox in the banner
prechecked_box.observed: At least one enabled checkbox inside the banner was already ticked when the page loaded.
prechecked_box.not_observed: No enabled, pre-ticked checkbox was found in the banner.
prechecked_box.why: Consent requires an active choice. Boxes that arrive ticked are the classic example of a default that does not amount to consent.
prechecked_box.caution: Checkboxes in a hidden second layer are counted even if the visitor never sees them. Boxes for strictly necessary cookies are often ticked and locked, so check the label before drawing a conclusion.

filled_vs_link.title: Accept styled as a filled button, reject styled differently
filled_vs_link.observed: The accept button has a filled background while the reject button does not (outlined or plain text).
filled_vs_link.not_observed: No difference in filled styling between accept and reject was measured.
filled_vs_link.why: Visual emphasis can steer a visitor toward one option. Regulators have described unequal presentation of the choices as a design pattern that can undermine free consent.
filled_vs_link.caution: Styling differences are common and are not unlawful by themselves. The measure reads computed CSS on the first accept and reject buttons it finds.

accept_more_contrast.title: Accept text has noticeably higher contrast
accept_more_contrast.observed: The text contrast of the accept button exceeds the reject button by at least 2.0 (WCAG contrast ratio).
accept_more_contrast.not_observed: No large text-contrast gap between the two buttons was measured.
accept_more_contrast.why: A faint reject button is harder to see and read, which can make refusal less likely.
accept_more_contrast.caution: This measures text against its background, not how much the whole button stands out. A prominent accept button with similar text contrast will not register.

accept_much_larger.title: Accept button is much larger
accept_much_larger.observed: The accept button's area is at least 1.5 times that of the reject button.
accept_much_larger.not_observed: No large size gap between the two buttons was measured.
accept_much_larger.why: A bigger target is easier to notice and to hit, and is one way presentation can favor acceptance.
accept_much_larger.caution: Area is measured from the rendered boxes at the current window size. Layouts change with viewport width.

confirmshaming.title: Guilt-tripping wording
confirmshaming.observed: Banner or button text matched a confirmshaming phrase (for example, a refusal phrased as a personal failing).
confirmshaming.not_observed: No confirmshaming phrase from the lexicon was found.
confirmshaming.why: Emotionally loaded refusal wording can pressure a visitor, which bears on whether consent is freely given.
confirmshaming.caution: The lexicon is a short list of English phrases. It will miss other wording and other languages.

implied_consent.title: Implied-consent wording
implied_consent.observed: The text says that continuing, scrolling or closing counts as agreement.
implied_consent.not_observed: No implied-consent phrase from the lexicon was found.
implied_consent.why: Consent needs a clear affirmative act. Continued browsing is generally not treated as one.
implied_consent.caution: The phrase may sit in a privacy notice rather than describe how consent is collected. Read the banner before concluding anything.

vague_purpose.title: Vague purpose wording
vague_purpose.observed: The text uses a generic purpose such as 'improve your experience' without naming specific purposes.
vague_purpose.not_observed: No vague-purpose phrase from the lexicon was found.
vague_purpose.why: Consent has to be specific and informed, so purposes should be named.
vague_purpose.caution: This is the least reliable signal in the evaluation. Specific purposes may be listed in a second layer that the tool does not read.

pressure.title: Pressure or urgency wording
pressure.observed: The text matched an urgency or obligation phrase such as 'you must accept'.
pressure.not_observed: No pressure phrase from the lexicon was found.
pressure.why: Consent that is presented as compulsory or urgent may not be freely given.
pressure.caution: A genuine statement that a service needs cookies to function can match. Check the context.

known_trackers.title: Known tracker domains contacted early
known_trackers.observed: During page load and the following four seconds, the page contacted domains on the Disconnect tracker list.
known_trackers.not_observed: No Disconnect-listed tracker domain was contacted in that window.
known_trackers.why: Reading or writing information on a device for non-essential purposes generally needs consent first. Contact with advertising or analytics hosts before any choice is a signal worth checking.
known_trackers.caution: A contact with a listed domain does not prove that identifiers were stored or read, or that the purpose was non-essential. If you accepted cookies on an earlier visit, this activity may be consent-based.

third_party_cookies.title: Third-party cookies set early
third_party_cookies.observed: During page load and the following four seconds, server responses set cookies for a domain other than the site's own.
third_party_cookies.not_observed: No third-party Set-Cookie response was seen in that window.
third_party_cookies.why: Third-party cookies set before a choice is made are a common source of consent problems.
third_party_cookies.caution: Only cookies set through HTTP response headers are seen. Cookies written by scripts are not counted. If you accepted cookies earlier, these cookies may be consent-based.
